statement: Denisovans were identified as a population distinct from both Neanderthals and modern humans primarily through ancient DNA — first a complete mitochondrial genome, then a nuclear genome — from a finger-bone fragment at Denisova Cave, Siberia, before any diagnostic morphological/skeletal type description existed. This is noted in the literature as an unusual, arguably first, case of a hominin lineage being defined by molecular data in the absence of a diagnostic fossil.

sources.citation: Krause, J. et al. "The complete mitochondrial DNA genome of an unknown hominin from southern Siberia." Nature 464: 894-897.
